one_line: Evidence-bound resume and application tailoring with human approval.
what_it_does: Lets an agent inspect a job posting and user fact bank, propose grounded resume and cover-letter diffs, and assemble an application without inventing experience or submitting without confirmation.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is the product's safety and collaboration boundary: the page exposes only currently permitted structured operations and grounded state, which a UI-driving agent could not reliably reproduce.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes 13 page-registered tools and changing capability boundary.
Every proposed edit cites source facts and the agent cannot apply edits itself.
Unregistered prepare_application is invisible while approval is pending.
execution_rationale: The transcript gives a coherent end-to-end workflow from fit checking through guarded diffs, cover letter validation, approval, and capability changes; frame evidence is visually thin and largely unreadable.
execution_evidence: 150-second video transcript covers fit check, refusal, diff review, acceptance, and submission gating.
Three frame sheets show a consistent dark application workspace and prompt/output progression.
Demo is reported alive and public repository exists.
impact_rationale: It addresses a concrete high-stakes problem for job applicants: fluent but unsupported claims entering applications, with meaningful protection for users bearing the consequences.
impact_evidence: Grounds claims in the applicant's recorded facts.
Handles unsupported technologies and boilerplate as ungrounded.
Human confirmation is required before application submission.
creativity_rationale: The concept makes the page, rather than the prompt or model, the authority over claims and agent permissions, and explicitly surfaces cross-project grounding limits.
creativity_evidence: Evidence-bound resume is a distinctive application of WebMCP.
Capability registration changes with workflow state.
The project deliberately exposes what it does not verify.
usability_note: The proposed-diff and evidence presentation is clear in the transcript; exact visual polish is difficult to assess from small contact sheets.
red_flags: Visual frame text is too small to independently verify details.
standouts: Page-enforced evidence boundary and human approval model.
advance_reason: Strong, differentiated WebMCP leverage with credible impact and a demonstrated central workflow.

leverage_rationale: Structured map state and domain actions make agent operation more reliable than clicking a map, but a capable UI agent could achieve much of the same outcome with friction.
leverage_evidence: Claims live map state is exposed directly to an agent.
Agent can rescore spots and create notes/weather watches.
Frame sheet visibly shows a map, list, and layer controls.
execution_rationale: The product scope is coherent and the demo is alive, but there is no submitted video and the frame sheets are repetitive and too low resolution to establish end-to-end completion.
execution_evidence: 211-spot map and gear scoring are clearly described.
Frame sheet shows a functioning geographic workspace.
No transcript or video completion evidence.
impact_rationale: Kitesurfers have a specific planning and safety-oriented need for conditions and gear-fit discovery; the niche audience still represents credible value.
impact_evidence: Real-time scoring against rider setup.
Weather watch and trip-planning direction.
211 spots across a global map.
creativity_rationale: A live sport map that re-scores locations for a personal quiver and supports agent-created watches is a fresh synthesis, though the underlying map category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Gear-specific scoring rather than generic spot browsing.
Agent operates map state and creates persistent actions.
usability_note: Map/list/layer layout appears usable, though exact labels are unreadable.
red_flags: No video or transcript; contact sheet is repetitive and low resolution.
advance_reason: Credible niche product with meaningful structured-state benefit, despite limited evidence.

leverage_rationale: Dynamic scaffolding and deterministic crisis-state transitions benefit substantially from structured in-page tools and shared state; generic UI driving is less reliable for safety-critical actions.

execution_evidence: Screenshot shows interaction canvas awaiting agent request.
Visible guardrails include drift score and sanitization status.
No submitted video or frame sheets.

one_line: Shared financial workspace where agents request changes and humans approve them.
what_it_does: Uses typed WebMCP tools to analyze spending, manage budgets, and request changes while keeping consequential mutations behind explicit human approval.
leverage_rationale: Shared live financial state, typed operations, and approval-gated mutation are materially more reliable and auditable than generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies typed tools and shared financial context.
Screenshots show agent mission, approvals, live filtered state, and tool activity.
Budget changes require approval before live state updates.
execution_rationale: Ten screenshots present a coherent product surface and architecture, but absent video means the central request-to-approval transition is claimed rather than observed.
execution_evidence: Gallery includes overview, charts, approval request, filtered state, and architecture views.

Demo is reported alive.
impact_rationale: Budget management and controlled financial actions serve a concrete audience with a real need for assistance without surrendering control.
impact_evidence: Live spending analysis and budget goals.
Approval workspace tracks decisions and requested changes.
Human remains responsible for sensitive mutations.
creativity_rationale: The human-controlled action pattern is well executed in a financial setting, though approval-gated agent actions are an increasingly familiar design.
creativity_evidence: Separates recommendation from mutation.
Shared agent/human workspace and explicit approval state.
usability_note: Screenshots suggest clear dashboards and approval surfaces.
red_flags: No video; interaction behavior is not independently demonstrated.
standouts: Concrete approval workflow for financial mutations.
advance_reason: Strong practical WebMCP integration and credible financial workflow.

one_line: Collaborative architecture diagram canvas edited by humans and agents together.
what_it_does: Lets an agent create and update structured architecture diagrams while humans drag, rename, connect, and delete nodes; the agent reads live state before changes and can export Mermaid.
leverage_rationale: Structured graph state is the core advantage: agents can address nodes and edges precisely instead of interpreting SVG/canvas pixels or overwriting human edits.
leverage_evidence: Ten explicit tools include get_diagram, add/update/remove_node, connect, layout, and export.
Agent reads the live canvas before every change.
Description states screenshots lose graph structure and the agent sees the same model as the human.
execution_rationale: The described central workflow is detailed and internally coherent, with a live demo and public code, but no video or frame evidence limits end-to-end certainty.
execution_evidence: Detailed tool list and human editing operations.
Claims nodes, edges, auto-layout, highlighting, and Mermaid export.
Demo URL and repository are provided.
impact_rationale: Software teams routinely need architecture diagrams, and reducing the friction between natural-language intent and an editable, shared graph has credible value.
impact_evidence: Supports services, databases, queues, caches, users, and labelled edges.
Human and agent edit the same model.
Mermaid export supports downstream documentation.
creativity_rationale: The live co-editing model, especially agent read-before-write behavior on a structured graph, is a strong and memorable WebMCP interaction.
creativity_evidence: Human edits remain visible to the agent without description overhead.
Read-only/destructive annotations and addressable node identity.
usability_note: The concept explicitly supports direct manipulation and visible agency, but no visual evidence was submitted.
red_flags: No screenshots or video in packet; core claims are unobserved.
standouts: Excellent fit between WebMCP structured state and graph editing.
advance_reason: One of the clearest cases where WebMCP changes agent reliability and collaboration.

Budget and alternative management.
